Trackmania finally hit mainstream, but only after donning the Ubisoft umbrella and going for a F2P/Subscription model, which feels like a little bit of a gut punch. The success of Trackmania is being carried by the community. A community that is overall very friendly and astonishingly dedicated. Competition is stronger than it has ever been before, and the game keeps getting better. The F2P model unfortunately greatly restricts the game's functionality, so if you don't want to pay for a subscription, the older Trackmania games are where you should start. If you do pay for a subscription, what you'll find is the most complex, engaging, social, and active version of Trackmania. Given the price, I think the subscription is worth it, but only because of all the content that the Trackmania community supplements the game with.

All that being said, this game does have many flaws. Every time that there's a new campaign of tracks, your Live Ranking for the campaign tracks is reset to Bronze 1, meaning that Bronze 1 is filled with both good experienced players and bad beginner players at the start of each season. There are numerous physics bugs that either remain in the game indefinitely or that require patches which creates discrepancies in what times are achievable on certain tracks. The user interface is poorly designed and I could easily see people having a hard time finding what they're looking for. The game also requires a Ubisoft Account.

PREFACE: While the game and community refers to the paid portion of the game as a "Subscription", it's not recurring. It's more like a battle-pass.

Fun arcade racer. High skill ceiling but relatively easy to learn. And it's free* to boot!

*While having to pay every year is a bummer, it's US$10** for a years-worth of content. If you don't want to spend money, however, the main part of the game (seasonal campaign tracks) is still available F2P. Overall, very fun game and low-ish price for virtually unlimited content

**Standard access is US$10, and gives you access to community-made maps and online play, such as Track of the Day, Ranked, and Royal. Club access is US$30, which is unnecessary unless you *really* get into the game. Adds skins and "club features" (ability to create your own campaigns and host rooms)

Overall, very good game, if a bit annoying on account of the yearly pass.

9/10, very much recommended to anyone interested in arcade racing

This game is "pay to get good."

The monetization model this game uses is having a free-to-play base (you can play some campaign maps and weekly shorts), and then some paid tiers. If you don't pay, you don't get access to the full campaign. Ranked multiplayer uses the campaign maps. Once you hit a certain rank, you start exclusively playing the campaign maps that you do not have access to without paying. Therefore, you cannot practice, and you get hardstuck in Silver II if you don't want to pay for a subscription. Ironically, because of this I have gold in the campaign maps I technically should have to pay for.

Also, this game has several Ubisoft warts, like in-game ads and requiring UPlay. (which is the worst piece of software I've ever had the displeasure of using, second only to every Microsoft product)

Is it fun though? Yeah, it's fun.

Trackmania is an arcade car racing game that is based on time trials and improving your score over and over in short maps with different landscapes. The game is enjoyable for a while, but the learning curve is pretty steep. I don't recommend the game because it is marketed as free to play, but most of the game's content is behind a paywall. The graphics, the UI, and the music are quite nice though. 7/10 overall.
